rows.explainer: Assumption Based on conversations with implementer, our best guess is that following the conclusion of the Global Fund-supported project, TPT coverage in districts supported by this project will revert mostly but not completely to the level in districts that were not supported by this project. We assume TPT coverage will be 20% higher in districts that received support from this project compared to those that did not.

rows.label: 2022 TPT initiation rate for under-5 HHCs of all notified PTB index patients, with higher coverage in districts that received support from the Global Fund-suppo
TPT initiation rate annual growth rate (Bihar)
rows.explainer: Assumption Implementer staff informed us that their best guess, given knowledge of timing of current programming and TPT coverage data quality, is a growth rate of 5-10% per year. We've adjusted these estimates upwards to put some weight on the possibility that the growth in TPT coverage reported in the 2023 India TB Report (p. 53, Figure 5.2) continues (note that Figure 5.2 includes all HHCs, not just under-5 HHCs, and the rapid increase may reflect expansion of TPT to the over-5 HHC group). We assume a faster growth rate for Bihar than Uttar Pradesh because of Bihar's lower starting point and potential for catch-up.

Adjustment factor for smaller effect from facility-based TPT initiation
rows.explainer: We guess that 80% of the benefits for under-5 are generated through initiation of TPT at the household rather than at the facility, and 20% from screening at the household

rows.label: Adjustment factor for higher counterfactual TB treatment coverage
rows.explainer: Guess - TB treatment rates are higher for adults than for young children, so preventing TB is less important for adults than children in terms of preventing deaths

rows.label: Adjustment factor for transmission effects
rows.explainer: We assume that each new case of TB disease generates 1 additional secondary case. This is roughly consistent with the range of 'R' estimates from studies reported here (Figure 4). We have not looked into whether R would be significantly lower for household contacts. This is not counted as a benefit for under-5 children because our impression is that transmission of TB by young children is relatively small.

rows.label: Adjustment factor for averted TB deaths being temporarily delayed rather than genuinely averted
rows.explainer: Guess - this is probably more of an issue for adults than for young children, because TB mortality profile in adults does not seem to decline quickly as they age, compared to children in the 0-5 age bucket (see Menzies et al 2021, Figure 1). So even if you avert TB disease and death over the program period, the same individual might be at relatively high risk of dying from TB in a subsequent year.

rows.explainer: GiveWell reports this model's result in multiples of cash transfers. Multiplying by GiveWell's value of a dollar to GiveDirectly converts it into units of value per dollar, so it ranks against the other models. Older sheets used older moral weights; the multiple of cash is the comparable number across years.
